newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip amid investor caution.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip amid investor caution.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Monday as players remained sidelined by a lack of market moving news and a backdrop of concerns over high-level corruption charges.

"The market did not express itself because of the political corruption concerns," said a trader at a large Argentine brokerage house, explaining that the recent corruption accusations have been used by investors as an excuse not to take new positions.
However, the trader added that extremely thin trading volumes, like those seen on Friday and Monday, usually result in softer prices.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.30 to 118.20, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 1/4 to 82-1/8.

Another trader said "the market has been reduced in general, the political noise from last week is still having repercussions in the market. Foreign investors are remaining cautious and are not changing their positions."

Traders said the market hesitated on former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo's testimony in court on alleged bribery involving state-owned bank Banco Nacion and the local branch of U.S. computer giant IBM.
Apart from the IBM-Banco Nacion scandal, Cavallo's charges last week that two government ministers manipulated courts and attempted to cover up corruption have increased political uncertainty.

Market players were unsure how long the uncertainty would be used by investors as a reason to shy away from the market even though few traders said they thought the corruption allegations would have any serious impact.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 7.55 percent from 7.60 percent Friday.
